chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Zayd Al-Shahham, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

The believer is not tested with anything harder for him than three characteristics which he must refrain from (or: which are obligatory), it was said: And what are they? He said: Generosity with one's own wealth for the sake of God, being just with oneself, and frequently remembering God. Indeed, I do not mean for you [to merely recite] 'Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar', but rather remembering God when He permits [actions], and remembering God when He forbids [actions] for you.
ai.seo_question: What are the three hardest tests for a believer according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three difficult but essential traits for believers: generosity with one's wealth, self-justice, and constant remembrance of God. He clarifies that true 'dhikr' is not merely reciting formulaic phrases, but maintaining God-consciousness in both permissible and forbidden matters. This teaching, found in *Al-Khisal*, emphasizes that spiritual success requires internalizing divine awareness in daily actions rather than relying solely on ritualistic recitation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-130 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Zayd al-Shoham that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

Nothing is a harder (divine) test for a believer than giving charity from what he has earned from God the Almighty, being just and frequently remembering God.” He (MGB) then said, “I do not mean that you should often recite praises of God, but remember God in what you do regarding what is allowed and what is forbidden.”
